question.problem: A party-planning company decorated a room with $200$ balloons. Of this amount, $7.5%$ of the balloons are white. How many white balloons are there?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the number of balloons in the room, which is $200.$ The percentage is $7.5%,$ and the part is the number of white balloons.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
7.5%=7.5÷100=0.075
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =7.5%\times 200 \\  & =0.075\times 200 \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $7.5%$ of $200$ is $15.$ Thus, there are $15$ white balloons.

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
7.5%=\frac{7.5}{100}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =7.5%\times 200 \\  & =\frac{7.5}{100}\times 200 \\  & =7.5\times \frac{200}{100} \\  & =7.5\times 2 \\  & =15\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $7.5%$ of $200$ is $15.$ Thus, there are $15$ white balloons.
